+| ID | Question | What we found | What stays open |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Q-01 | What qualifies as a small runnable application? | C, The task, requires a “small runnable application”; C, What to submit, requires a supported runtime in README.md. | Required operating systems, resource budget and application-size limit. |
+| Q-02 | What makes the interface suited to the IT team? | C, The task, explicitly allows a CLI, service or web application. | Acceptance criteria for suitability beyond the stated operator actions. |
+| Q-03 | What must completed-result inspection expose? | C, The task, requires inspection while other requests are pending; D, Record and review behavior, requires status, owner and next action. | Additional required detail, filtering, ordering and inspection freshness. |
+| Q-04 | What belongs in the review queue, and in what order? | P, Review queue and Processing and recovery, defines routed results and requires the latest attempt's error in the current queue. | Queue ordering, filtering and representation of pending work. |
+| Q-05 | What is the outer extraction-record format? | C, What to submit, names envelope fields; S defines the extraction object rather than that envelope. | Envelope field types, nested structures and extra-field rules. |
+| Q-06 | How is response_source encoded? | C, What to submit, permits `mock` or the provider and model ID that produced the record. | String versus object representation and the provider/model naming convention. |
+| Q-07 | What is response_source when no response is produced? | C requires response_source on current records; P defines extraction-failure outputs. | Its value when configuration fails, no call occurs or the provider returns no model response. |
+| Q-08 | What is the JSON structure of queue.json? | C, What to submit, requires a review queue linked by document_id; P supplies routing values. | Top-level JSON type, complete entry structure and additional required fields. |
+| Q-09 | How does a queue entry identify its exact extraction version? | C links entries by document_id; D, Shared operations, requires queue and extraction agreement about source version. | Revision/attempt linkage beyond document_id and how that agreement is represented. |
+| Q-10 | What form should implemented response handling take in request-evidence.json? | C, What to submit, requests an example model request “plus the implemented response handling.” | Description, response examples, code references or another representation. |
+| Q-11 | How broad must runtime/provider support be? | C requires a supported runtime/provider; D, Record and review behavior, requires a documented supported configuration and configurable settings. | Required compatibility breadth beyond the documented configuration. |
+| Q-12 | What counts as a recorded observation, and what configuration must accompany it? | C, Submission, requires each recorded observation to identify configuration and mock/provider use. | Which artifacts count as observations and the minimum configuration detail per label. |
+| Q-13 | What does repairs mean in verification.md? | C, What to submit, requires observed results or repairs to be clearly identified. | Whether repairs include code fixes, data fixes, extraction corrections or all of these. |
+| Q-14 | How is session capture paired with the submitted commit? | C, What to submit and Submission, delegates capture setup and instructions to the facilitator. | Capture format, destination and pairing mechanism within these four files. |
+| Q-15 | What performance must ordinary and burst intake achieve? | D, Workload and the review day, gives approximately 200–400 daily messages and a roughly 2,000-message morning intake; D, Verification, requires workload assumptions. | Completion deadlines, throughput and resource targets; R-90 documents assumptions without a performance threshold. |
+| Q-16 | When is a response slow or failed? | D, Workload and the review day and Service interruptions and handover, describes slow responses and outages. | Timeouts and thresholds for delay, failure and recovery. |
+| Q-17 | Must other extractions progress while one response is slow? | D, Workload and the review day, says a slow response should leave other work available; R-05 checks completed-result inspection. | Whether availability also requires other extractions to keep progressing and what progress is sufficient. |
+| Q-18 | How must intake adapt to changing provider capacity? | D describes shared model access and variable request rates and response times. | Required concurrency limits, rate controls and adaptation behavior. |
+| Q-19 | What shared deployment topology must be supported? | D, Shared operations, says regional operators use the same records. | Shared process, shared filesystem, separate hosts or regional deployments. |
+| Q-20 | Are duplicate model calls acceptable during overlapping intake? | D, Shared operations, anticipates two operators starting around the same time; P requires one current entry per document on unchanged reruns. | Whether duplicate provider calls are permitted if current outputs remain coherent. |
+| Q-21 | What consistency must concurrent readers observe? | D requires a “coherent current queue” and source-version agreement; R-06–R-08 repeat those outcomes. | Whether mixed revisions may be transiently visible and the required consistency boundary. |
+| Q-22 | What makes earlier activity trustworthy? | D, Shared operations, requires a “trustworthy record of earlier activity.” | Required audit events, attribution, timestamps and protection against modification. |
+| Q-23 | Which interruptions must recovery tolerate? | D mentions deployments, service outages and model-service interruptions. | Required coverage of process termination, machine failure, storage failure and provider outage. |
+| Q-24 | At what point is work completed durably? | D requires distinguishing completed from unfinished work and resuming recorded state. | Whether completion requires response receipt, extraction persistence, queue persistence or all of them. |
+| Q-25 | How is interrupted in-flight work resumed? | D, Shared operations, requires continuation from recorded state without losing completed work. | Reclaiming abandoned work, detecting active workers and whether in-flight model calls may be repeated. |
+| Q-26 | How is the latest source ordered? | D, Updates and follow-up, refers to later exports and the latest processed source. | Arrival order, exported_at, processing-start order or processing-completion order. |
+| Q-27 | Which result wins when revisions finish out of order? | D requires the latest processed source in the current view and coherent shared records. | Whether an older revision finishing later may replace a newer revision and how precedence is established. |
+| Q-28 | What does the current view show during refresh? | D requires current results, visible new failures and distinguishable unfinished work. | Whether pending refresh replaces the prior current result or is displayed alongside it. |
+| Q-29 | How much history must be retained? | D requires earlier results/activity; P requires earlier versions and the last valid result after failure. | Retention duration, size limits and whether all unsuccessful attempts must be retained. |
+| Q-30 | Which processing settings invalidate reuse? | D, Record and review behavior, says “relevant processing settings”; R-12–R-13 and R-80 depend on that term. | Exact inclusion of provider, model, prompt, schema, policy, sampling settings, endpoint and application version. |
+| Q-31 | How are affected results selected and refreshed? | D, Updates and follow-up, requires refresh when configuration or policy affects production or routing; R-12 checks this outcome. | Automatic versus explicit refresh, selection rules and whether policy-only changes require another model call. |
+| Q-32 | How is a policy version identified? | D requires operators to understand which policy version produced records; R-13 requires provenance inspection. | Version format, derivation and handling of policy edits without an explicit version field. |
+| Q-33 | Does unchanged-result reuse apply to failures? | D requires reuse when source/settings are unchanged; P requires explicit failure and retry behavior. | Whether an unchanged failed result is reused, automatically retried or retried only explicitly. |
+| Q-34 | What must a reproducible retry reproduce? | D requires a reproducible retry command; R-83 checks that it creates a new attempt. | Repeatable invocation versus identical result, and whether retry uses original or current source/settings. |
+| Q-35 | What is the complete input export contract? | P, Input export format, specifies UTF-8 JSON, a message string and descriptive metadata fields. | Required metadata, metadata types, supported export_version values and extra-field handling. |
+| Q-36 | How are invalid or unreadable exports handled? | P describes valid UTF-8 JSON exports; its failure rule addresses extraction failure. | Handling of invalid JSON/UTF-8, missing or non-string message values and unreadable files. |
+| Q-37 | Is 200 English words a validation limit or an input-domain description? | P says messages vary in length up to 200 English words; R-35 interprets this as supported input length. | Word-count definition and behavior for longer or non-English messages, including whether rejection is intended. |
+| Q-38 | What exactly is the filename used as document_id? | P explicitly uses the input filename for document_id. | Basename versus relative path, case sensitivity and collisions across directories. |
+| Q-39 | How is the identifier in a filename parsed? | P requires detecting a mismatch between the message identifier and filename identifier. | Filename grammar and which substring is the request identifier. |
+| Q-40 | What does renaming an input file mean? | P uses filename identity and treats each message as an independent document. | Whether a rename creates another document or can represent a revision of an existing document. |
+| Q-41 | Which identifier in a message is request_id? | P says to retain the stated identifier and report filename mismatch. | Selection when several IDs appear, including references to other requests. |
+| Q-42 | How is a message containing multiple requests represented? | P treats one exported message as one independent document; S provides one set of scalar request facts. | Whether to select a request, report unresolved facts or reject extraction when a message requests multiple systems, permissions or beneficiaries. |
+| Q-43 | Which date is request_date? | P requires request_date and prohibits deriving business facts from the export timestamp. | Distinction between message-writing date, submission date and a prior request date mentioned in the message. |
+| Q-44 | Who is requester when someone requests access for another person? | P and S name requester without defining its role. | Sender, person making the request or access beneficiary. |
+| Q-45 | Whose team is extracted? | P and S require team. | Requester's team, beneficiary's team or responsible system team. |
+| Q-46 | What granularity and naming apply to system? | P and S require system as a nullable string. | Application versus subsystem and normalization of aliases or abbreviations. |
+| Q-47 | Who is manager, and what identification is sufficient? | P requires manager for complete new/change requests and defines a named manager as a contact. | Whose manager is meant and whether names, roles or contact details suffice. |
+| Q-48 | Is business_purpose quoted or summarized? | P requires explicit facts and a business_purpose value; exactness is explicitly required for supporting_quotes. | Verbatim extraction versus faithful summarization of purpose. |
+| Q-49 | How are request kinds classified? | P and S permit new, change, withdrawal, other and null. | Boundary between other and null and classification of messages mixing several kinds. |
+| Q-50 | How are source expressions mapped to environment and permission enums? | S limits environment and permission values; P requires extraction from explicit facts. | Accepted synonyms, abbreviations and mappings such as prod, view access or read/write. |
+| Q-51 | How are explicit values outside the enums handled? | S excludes unlisted environment and permission values; P requires null for unresolved facts. | Whether an unsupported source value becomes null with an issue, affects kind or causes extraction failure. |
+| Q-52 | How much inference is consistent with explicit facts? | P says “Use explicit facts from each message.” | Permitted abbreviation expansion, normalization and interpretation of implied facts. |
+| Q-53 | What makes a fact uncertain or unresolved? | D requires uncertain fields to be null with an issue; P uses absent/unresolved language. | Confidence threshold or decision procedure for uncertainty. |
+| Q-54 | Do empty strings and placeholders count as missing? | S accepts strings without minimum lengths; P requires missing scalar facts to be null with issues. | Treatment of whitespace, empty strings and placeholders such as unknown or TBD. |
+| Q-55 | What constitutes conflicting details? | P requires unresolved contradictions and clarification routing for conflicts. | Boundary between contradiction, compatible descriptions and additional detail. |
+| Q-56 | What qualifies as an explicitly labelled correction? | P lets a later explicitly labelled correction replace an earlier value. | Accepted correction language, ordering inside quoted/forwarded text and precedence among several corrections. |
+| Q-57 | Must evidence retain superseded values after a correction? | P requires corrected values to replace earlier ones and conflicting alternatives to remain in quotes. | Whether corrected-away values still need quotes or issues. |
+| Q-58 | What counts as a relative date? | P says a relative date stays unresolved. | Treatment of weekdays, partially specified dates, immediately, ongoing and dates relative to an explicit anchor. |
+| Q-59 | How are source dates normalized? | P requires YYYY-MM-DD and prohibits resolving relative dates. | Ambiguous numeric dates, omitted years, timestamps and timezone conversion. |
+| Q-60 | What happens to a date that has the right shape but is impossible? | P requires YYYY-MM-DD; S only checks string/null types and has no date format constraint. | Calendar-validity checking and whether invalid dates cause extraction failure or clarification. |
+| Q-61 | How are change requests affecting fields other than permission extracted? | P explicitly says to extract the requested new permission for change requests. | Whether other fields describe existing state or requested new state when system, environment or dates change. |
+| Q-62 | How much supporting evidence is required? | P defines exact quotes as decoded-message substrings and requires conflicting alternatives to be preserved. | Minimum field coverage, quote length, order, duplicates and whether empty quote arrays can suffice. |
+| Q-63 | What conventions apply to issues? | S defines an array of strings; P requires explanations of missing/conflicting facts and override attempts. | Free-text versus structured conventions, association with fields, ordering and wording expectations. |
+| Q-64 | Which schema-validation rules and semantic boundary apply? | S declares object properties, types, enums, required keys and no additional properties, but no dialect; P adds semantic rules. | JSON Schema dialect and the complete boundary between structural failure and a business-fact issue. |
+| Q-65 | What is an instruction-override attempt? | P, Review queue rule 1, defines its route and evidence requirements. | Classification of malicious overrides versus quoted examples, ordinary request instructions or harmless discussion. |
+| Q-66 | Who detects routing conditions? | P requires ordered routing after validation; S has no dedicated override or conflict flags. | Model versus application responsibility for detecting overrides, conflicts and other routing conditions. |
+| Q-67 | Where must override source evidence be stored? | P says to keep the attempted instruction as source evidence; R-65 checks evidence and issues. | Whether supporting_quotes is mandatory or retained original text/another artifact suffices. |
+| Q-68 | Which route applies when override-message extraction fails? | P places routing after extraction validation and separately defines extraction-failure routing. | Whether failed extraction always produces error or an independently detected override can produce inspect-message. |
+| Q-69 | What makes a withdrawal's request_id and request_date usable? | P's ordered rule 2 precedes the conflict/mismatch clarification rule. | Whether disputed, malformed or otherwise invalid ID/date values satisfy rule 2; rule ordering itself is explicit. |
+| Q-70 | Which facts are required for an incomplete withdrawal? | P requires ID/date for confirmation routing but lists required facts only for new/change requests. | The explicit required-fact set and fallback evaluation for withdrawals missing ID or date. |
+| Q-71 | How is required fact distinguished from required schema key? | S requires all property keys; P requires non-null business facts for new/change routing and separately handles kind other/null. | Whether kind is treated as a required business fact and the precise completeness predicate. |
+| Q-72 | Can other issues coexist with complete-request routing? | P enumerates clarification conditions; it does not state that every issue triggers clarification. | Treatment of issues outside the listed missing/conflicting/mismatch/date-order conditions. |
+| Q-73 | Does involving production, write or admin refer only to requested access? | P, Review queue rule 4, uses “involving”; change-request extraction specifically selects the new permission. | Whether existing access or incidental mentions also trigger Security Review. |
+| Q-74 | How are named reviewers and system owners identified? | D reserves approval for named human reviewers; P routes to IT Service Desk, Security Review or System Owner. | Role-label ownership versus individual assignment and any system-to-owner directory. |
+| Q-75 | Does the application implement the Security Review handoff? | P describes risk review followed by a recommendation to the system owner and calls the application output a review queue. | Whether the application only labels the next action or supports workflow transitions and forwarding. |
+| Q-76 | Does a withdrawal change other documents for the same request? | P treats messages as independent documents and routes withdrawals for human confirmation; D says absence from a batch is not withdrawal. | Whether withdrawal intake changes earlier queue entries or leaves all cross-document effects to human review. |
+| Q-77 | Which provider signals establish completion, refusal or interruption? | D explicitly requires validation of completion and handling of refusal/interrupted responses. | Accepted provider-specific statuses and treatment of partial content, truncation and mixed refusal/content. |
+| Q-78 | What retry policy is required for provider problems? | D requires explicit handling and resumption; P requires an error route and retry action. | Automatic retry, retryable categories, attempt limits, backoff and timeout policy. |
+| Q-79 | What makes an error actionable? | P requires an actionable error with retry-extraction. | Required error structure, diagnostic information and recovery guidance. |
+| Q-80 | What falls within extraction failure? | P defines its output; D explicitly lists malformed output, provider errors, refusal and interrupted responses. | Inclusion of invalid input, configuration problems, persistence failures and routing failures. |
+| Q-81 | What does separate storage of prior versions require? | P says prior versions must be stored separately from current outputs. | Physical separation into files/directories versus logical separation in a database or other store. |
